idiom_name: pydantic v2 discriminated (tagged) union: Field(discriminator=...) over Literal-typed members
implementation_notes: The standard library offers no type-directed decoding (json.loads returns dicts) - except pickle, which reconstructs arbitrary classes and is documented as insecure - so the practical realization is pydantic v2's discriminated union: every member model declares the tag as a Literal, and the annotated union validates only the member whose tag matched, which is both faster than trial validation and produces one precise error instead of a pile of unrelated ones. Where tags must map to non-pydantic constructors (plugin loading, per-type migrations), the handwritten dict from tag to callable is still the right shape - keep it explicit and reject unknown tags instead of falling through to a generic branch.
code_sketch:
class OrderCreated(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["order.created"]
    id: str
    total: int

class OrderCancelled(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["order.cancelled"]
    id: str
    reason: str

Event = Annotated[Union[OrderCreated, OrderCancelled], Field(discriminator="type")]
event = TypeAdapter(Event).validate_json(payload)   # tag selects the model
pitfalls: Never unpickle untrusted payloads: pickle.loads executes whatever the stream asks for - the documentation says so explicitly - which is this pattern's mechanism turned into an attack; the same caution applies to yaml.load with a non-safe loader.
An untagged Union validates members left to right and can coerce a payload into the wrong model; the discriminator is what removes that ambiguity.

Discriminated unions need the tag to be a Literal on every member and support only one discriminator field, so recursive or nested unions require an explicit Discriminator callable, and an unknown tag fails validation rather than routing to an unknown-type bucket.
